decisions.title: Tokens travel only in the Authorization header and never in cookies.
Sessions use one long-lived access token and the API has no refresh tokens.
Access tokens are signed with the HS256 algorithm using one shared secret key.
The Authorization header must use the prefix "Token", not "Bearer".
Invalid tokens and tokens for unknown users are rejected with 403 Forbidden and the same MALFORMED_PAYLOAD message.
Every access token carries the fixed subject claim access.
Registering with a username or email that is already taken is answered with HTTP 400.
The JWT payload identifies the user by username, not by numeric id.
Access tokens expire one week after issue and there is no refresh token.
Login returns one identical 400 error for an unknown email and for a wrong password.
Passwords are hashed with bcrypt through a passlib CryptContext.
Only an article's author, matched by username, may modify the article.
bcrypt keeps the default passlib work factor.
Only an article's author may update or delete it, checked by comparing usernames.
Each user gets a random salt created with bcrypt.gensalt.
Request validation failures return HTTP 422 with an errors list of the validator's error objects.
A separate per-user salt is stored in the users table and prepended to the password before bcrypt hashing.
Cross-origin calls are allowed from the origins in allowed_hosts, which default to every origin.
Password reset links stay valid for 30 minutes.
The fancyhash package is not used for password hashing because of its licence.
Favoriting an article sends no notification to its author.
Creating an article whose generated slug already exists is refused with HTTP 400.
updated_at is maintained by a PostgreSQL BEFORE UPDATE trigger, not by application code.
Changing an article's title regenerates its slug, so the article URL changes.
An article's slug is derived only from its title with python-slugify, and duplicate titles are rejected.
Article listing defaults to 20 items with a minimum limit of 1 and no maximum.
Deleting a user keeps their articles and sets author_id to NULL, while comments, favorites and follows cascade.
articlesCount in list responses is the length of the returned page, not the total number of matching articles.
Deleted articles and comments are removed from the database, with no soft-delete flag.
All API models expose camelCase JSON field names generated from snake_case attributes.
Database access uses raw SQL files loaded by aiosql over asyncpg, not an ORM.
Queries are hand-written SQL files, not generated by an ORM.
Creating a tag that already exists is ignored by the insert statement.
The article list defaults to 20 items per page.
The database pool is fixed at 10 connections through min_connection_count and max_connection_count.
PostgreSQL is the data store and MongoDB was not chosen.
